answer: Sybil rings collapse when each identity must prove fresh cognitive work every epoch. The ledger keeps an atlas of an author's past answers, and a new reply to the unpredictable prompt is machine-checked against it. Merely re-skinning an old text — swapping a word of pigment here, a stale fable there — is flagged as recycled and earns nothing. Minting a thousand fakes buys nothing if none can produce a thousand genuinely novel thoughts.
